name: A day at the coffee shop
needsNote: Order Desk closed. RabbitMQ running on this computer for part 7, the warehouse; without it, part 7 ships the order without one.
covers: A whole day in Order Desk in eight parts, each ending in a checkpoint: sign in, take an order, a rush of orders from a sheet, change and delete orders, the catalogue, the database, the warehouse over RabbitMQ, and the end-of-day export, leaving the computer as it was

steps.say: AutoTestRunner is about to test Order Desk, a coffee shop's ordering app, all by itself. It moves the mouse and types as a person would, and checks every result.

args: $c = New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient; try { if ($c.ConnectAsync('localhost', 5672).Wait(3000)) { 'answering' } } catch { } finally { $c.Close() }
if.label: RabbitMQ answers on this computer

steps.note: Order Desk reads its broker when it starts, so this is decided before it does. Part 7 uses the warehouse only when RabbitMQ answers.

steps.say: Point Order Desk at this computer's RabbitMQ, which plays the warehouse

else.say: RabbitMQ isn't running here, so Order Desk keeps the shop's own warehouse

steps.say: Part 1 of 8: Sign in. First with a wrong password, which Order Desk must turn away.
A wrong password. Passwords are never shown or written to the log.

steps.equals: The user name or password is wrong.

steps.say: Turned away, as it should be. Now the right password.

steps.checkpoint: Part 1: only the right password gets in

checks.to: Ready. Signed in as Jo Bloggs. 0 orders in ${dataDir}.
checks.label: Order Desk says who signed in
The shop's name, as Order Desk's own settings file has it

checks.sql: select FullName from Staff where UserName = @user
checks.label: Jo Bloggs is the clerk, in the database

look: The top bar says Contoso Coffee and Tea · Jo Bloggs.

steps.say: Part 2 of 8: Take an order over the phone. Watch each box being filled in.

steps.checkpoint: Part 2: Ada's order is on the list, and saved

checks.label: Order Desk says it was added

checks.sql: select Customer || ', ' || Quantity || ' x ' || Product from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved in the database

checks.sql: select Delivery from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved delivery

checks.sql: select Total from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved total

checks.sql: select Notes from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved note

checks.contains: Added order 1001: Ada Lovelace, 2 x Coffee beans, 35.00
checks.label: Written in the activity log

look: Order 1001 on the list: Ada Lovelace, 2 × Coffee beans, gift wrapped, next day, £35.00.

steps.say: Part 3 of 8: The lunchtime rush. Three more orders, one after another, read from a sheet.

steps.checkpoint: Part 3: the rush is taken, each order with its own number

checks.sql: select Total from Orders where Number = 1003
checks.label: Alan's mug, gift wrapped

steps.say: Part 4 of 8: Customers change their minds. Alan wants two mugs and the full name on his gift note, and Grace cancels her order.
Put the full name in the gift note
Delete only shows while the mouse is over the order
Order Desk asks first; the test checks the question before answering Yes

steps.checkpoint: Part 4: Alan's order is changed, and Grace's is gone

checks.label: Order Desk says it was saved

checks.sql: select Quantity from Orders where Number = 1003
checks.label: Saved quantity

checks.sql: select Notes from Orders where Number = 1003
checks.equals: Gift note: Happy birthday, Joan Clarke
checks.label: Saved gift note

checks.sql: select Number from Orders where Number = 1002
checks.label: Grace's order in the database

steps.say: Part 5 of 8: The catalogue. Drag a tea onto the order form, then find one spare part among 420, in a list that only builds the rows on screen.
Drag it onto the Product box of the order form
It scrolls until the part is built, far down the list

steps.checkpoint: Part 5: the tea is on the order form, and the part was found

checks.label: Order Desk says it was picked

steps.say: Part 6 of 8: Behind the scenes. The test adds a customer straight into the database, as the shop's customer system does overnight, and Order Desk must show her.

steps.sql: insert into Customers (Account, Name, Email) values (@account, @name, @email)
steps.say: As the overnight customer sync would add her
F5 has Order Desk read everything again

steps.checkpoint: Part 6: Hedy Lamarr shows up, straight from the database

checks.label: Order Desk says what it read
The new customer, on the Customers tab
Takings so far, added up by the database: £35 + £14 + £24

steps.say: Part 7 of 8: Ship Ada's order. Order Desk tells the warehouse through RabbitMQ, a message queue. The test plays the warehouse: it reads the message, then answers that the order is picked.
Start with no messages waiting

steps.checkpoint: Part 7: Ada's order is waiting for the warehouse

checks.to: Connected to the warehouse at localhost.
checks.label: Order Desk is connected

checks.to: Order 1001 shipped, and sent to the warehouse.
checks.label: Order Desk says it was sent

checks.sql: select Status from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved as shipped

steps.say: Take the message off the queue, as the warehouse would
Answer as the warehouse does once it has picked the order

steps.checkpoint: Part 7: the warehouse has picked Ada's order

checks.label: The message asked for 2 × Coffee beans

checks.sql: select Status from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved as picked

look: Order 1001 has a blue Picked label.

else.say: Part 7 of 8: Ship Ada's order. RabbitMQ, the message queue the warehouse uses, isn't running on this computer, so Order Desk just marks it shipped. The launcher offers to install RabbitMQ.

checks.label: Order Desk says it was shipped

checks.sql: select Status from Orders where Number = 1001
checks.label: Saved as shipped

look: Order 1001 has a green Shipped label.

steps.say: Part 8 of 8: End of the day. Export the orders to a file, check the file adds up, then put the computer back as it was.

steps.text: Exports from the Order Desk showcase. It deletes this folder when it ends.

steps.say: Export only works once the orders are checked
A script reads the file back, as a person checking it would
Point Order Desk back at the shop's own warehouse
Forget what Order Desk remembered

steps.checkpoint: The end: nothing is left behind

checks.label: Order Desk points at the shop's warehouse
Nothing else left on this computer

look: That was a whole day at the shop, tested in a few minutes. The results folder has a log of every step, and a report CI can read.
